Subject: [PATCH] clk: samsung: gs101: propagate PERIC1 USI SPI clock rate
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

When SPI transfer is being prepared, the spi-s3c64xx driver will call
clk_set_rate() to change the rate of SPI source clock (IPCLK). But IPCLK
is a gate (leaf) clock, so it must propagate the rate change up the
clock tree, so that corresponding MUX/DIV clocks can actually change
their values. Add CLK_SET_RATE_PARENT flag to corresponding clocks for
all USI instances in GS101 PERIC1: USI{0, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13}. This change
involves the following clocks:

PERIC1 USI*:

    Clock                              Div range    MUX Selection

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/clk/samsung/clk-gs101.c`**
   - **MUX Clocks**: The existing `MUX` definitions for the clocks `CLK_MOUT_PERIC1_USI{0, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13}_USI_USER` were changed to `nMUX`, indicating a modification in how these clocks are defined.
   - **DIV Clocks**: The `DIV` definitions for the clocks `CLK_DOUT_PERIC1_USI{0, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13}_USI` were replaced with `DIV_F` definitions, which now include the `CLK_SET_RATE_PARENT` flag, allowing the rate change to propagate up the clock tree.
   - **GATE Clocks**: The `GATE` definitions for the clocks `CLK_GOUT_PERIC1_PERIC1_TOP0_IPCLK_{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}` were modified to include the `CLK_SET_RATE_PARENT` flag, ensuring that these gates also propagate the clock rate changes.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modifications in the MUX, DIV, and GATE clocks are interconnected as they all pertain to the USI instances in the GS101 PERIC1 clock domain. By adding the `CLK_SET_RATE_PARENT` flag to the DIV and GATE clocks, the patch ensures that when the SPI source clock rate is changed via `clk_set_rate()`, the changes will propagate correctly through the clock tree, affecting all related MUX and DIV clocks. This ensures that the clock configuration is consistent and that the SPI transfer operates at the intended clock rate.

Here is the commit message:
clk: samsung: gs101: propagate PERIC1 USI SPI clock rate
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

When SPI transfer is being prepared, the spi-s3c64xx driver will call
clk_set_rate() to change the rate of SPI source clock (IPCLK). But IPCLK
is a gate (leaf) clock, so it must propagate the rate change up the
clock tree, so that corresponding MUX/DIV clocks can actually change
their values. Add CLK_SET_RATE_PARENT flag to corresponding clocks for
all USI instances in GS101 PERIC1: USI{0, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13}. This change
involves the following clocks:

PERIC1 USI*:

    Clock                              Div range    MUX Selection
    -------------------------------------------------------------------
    gout_peric1_peric1_top0_ipclk_*    -            -
    dout_peric1_usi*_usi               /1..16       -
    mout_peric1_usi*_usi_user          -            {24.5 MHz, 400 MHz}

With input clock of 400 MHz this scheme provides the following IPCLK
rate range, for each USI block:

    PERIC1 USI*:       1.5 MHz ... 400 MHz

Accounting for internal /4 divider in SPI blocks, and because the max
SPI frequency is limited at 50 MHz, it gives us next SPI SCK rates:

    PERIC1 USI_SPI*:   384 KHz ... 49.9 MHz

Which shall be fine for the applications of the SPI bus.

Note that with this we allow the reparenting of the MUX_USIx clocks to
OSCCLK. Each instance of the USI IP has its own MUX_USI clock, thus the
reparenting of a MUX_USI clock corresponds to a single instance of the
USI IP. The datasheet mentions OSCCLK just in the low-power mode
context, but the downstream driver reparents too the MUX_USI clocks to
OSCCLK. Follow the downstream driver and do the same.

Fixes: 2999e786d7e9 ("clk: samsung: gs101: add support for cmu_peric1")
Reviewed-by: Peter Griffin <peter.griffin@linaro.org>
Acked-by: André Draszik <andre.draszik@linaro.org>
Signed-off-by: Tudor Ambarus <tudor.ambarus@linaro.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240419100915.2168573-3-tudor.ambarus@linaro.org
Signed-off-by: Krzysztof Kozlowski <krzysztof.kozlowski@linaro.org>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug is that the SPI source clock (IPCLK) is a gate clock, and when its rate is changed using `clk_set_rate()`, the change does not propagate up the clock tree to the corresponding MUX and DIV clocks. This results in the MUX and DIV clocks not reflecting the updated clock rate, which can lead to incorrect clock configurations during SPI transfers.

        clk: samsung: gs101: propagate PERIC1 USI SPI clock rate
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

When SPI transfer is being prepared, the spi-s3c64xx driver will call
clk_set_rate() to change the rate of SPI source clock (IPCLK). But IPCLK
is a gate (leaf) clock, so it must propagate the rate change up the
clock tree, so that corresponding MUX/DIV clocks can actually change
their values. Add CLK_SET_RATE_PARENT flag to corresponding clocks for
all USI instances in GS101 PERIC1: USI{0, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13}. This change
involves the following clocks:

PERIC1 USI*:

    Clock                              Div range    MUX Selection
    -------------------------------------------------------------------
    gout_peric1_peric1_top0_ipclk_*    -            -
    dout_peric1_usi*_usi               /1..16       -
    mout_peric1_usi*_usi_user          -            {24.5 MHz, 400 MHz}

With input clock of 400 MHz this scheme provides the following IPCLK
rate range, for each USI block:

    PERIC1 USI*:       1.5 MHz ... 400 MHz

Accounting for internal /4 divider in SPI blocks, and because the max
SPI frequency is limited at 50 MHz, it gives us next SPI SCK rates:

    PERIC1 USI_SPI*:   384 KHz ... 49.9 MHz

Which shall be fine for the applications of the SPI bus.

Note that with this we allow the reparenting of the MUX_USIx clocks to
OSCCLK. Each instance of the USI IP has its own MUX_USI clock, thus the
reparenting of a MUX_USI clock corresponds to a single instance of the
USI IP. The datasheet mentions OSCCLK just in the low-power mode
context, but the downstream driver reparents too the MUX_USI clocks to
OSCCLK. Follow the downstream driver and do the same.
